chunk_findings.detail: The module and the acceptance criteria state that every refusal names the nearest verb, but several validation refusals do not. For example, with `[records].correct_reason_max_chars` set to its configured limit, `ddflow correct TASK-1 --field body --text x --reason <reason longer than the limit>` returns the failure from `_check_request` ending with “Say why it was wrong, not what it said.” and never includes `NEAREST` (`ddflow correct <id> --field NAME --text TEXT --reason WHY`). The same omission occurs when `len(fields) > rc.correct_max_fields`, so the CLI/MCP user is not told the nearest verb for those refusals.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/record_correct.py:_check_request

chunk_findings.detail: `_author` does not respect the record kind selected by `_resolve_kind`, even though `_resolve_kind` explicitly supports the same `rid` existing as more than one correctable kind. `_author` accepts any event whose prefix is in `(kind, "task", "phase", "item")`. Given a subject `X` that is both a task and a phase, if agent A created the task event for `X` first and agent B created the phase event for `X` later, then `ddflow correct X --kind phase ...` from agent B resolves the kind to `phase`, but `_author` can return agent A from the earlier task event. Agent B is then treated as not the author and may be refused despite correcting its own phase record; conversely agent A may be allowed to correct agent B’s phase record as the “author.” This violates the D-correction-permissions-2 rule that an agent may correct its own record without asking.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/record_correct.py:_author

chunk_findings.detail: The new common-field loop in `_h_updated` assigns `author_model` whenever the key is present, including when its value is falsey (`None` or `""`). The completion branch immediately below then tries to ignore falsey author values with `ev.data.get("author_model") or ev.data.get("author_family") or it.author_model`, but that fallback can no longer recover the previous author because the common loop has already overwritten `it.author_model` with the falsey value. Given an update/completion event whose data contains `{"author_model": ""}` or `{"author_model": null}` (for example, an unknown/omitted author serialized as empty), the item’s recorded author_model is cleared instead of preserved, contrary to the `or` fallback’s intent.

chunk_findings.detail: `_text_of` only catches `OSError` when reading `--from-file`. If the file exists and is readable but its bytes are not valid in the default encoding, `Path(path).read_text()` raises `UnicodeDecodeError` (a `ValueError`, not an `OSError`). For example, `ddflow correct BUG-1 --field body --from-file /tmp/binary.bin --reason typo` with a file containing invalid UTF-8 will propagate an uncaught traceback instead of returning a refusal such as “cannot read ...” plus the nearest verb. This also applies to valid UTF-16 files when the default encoding is UTF-8.

chunk_findings.detail: `_permission` canonicalizes the approval request without the actual new field values (or the `secret` choice): `target` is only the sorted field names and `state` only digests `kind:rid:names`; `args` only carries `kind` and `reason`. Therefore an operator approval obtained for one correction is accepted for a different correction of the same record/fields/reason. Example: an agent asks approval to correct task `T` body to `hello` with `secret= [REDACTED] the operator approves. The agent reruns the same approval with `--field body --text <secret>` and `--secret`; `_permission` builds the same Canon, `operator_gate` accepts, and the code writes the new secret and turns digests off. This violates D-correction-permissions-2’s “exactly this correction” requirement and defeats the audit opt-in for secrets.

chunk_findings.detail: For `secret= [REDACTED] the code computes `bound = D.content_digest(names)`, which does not bind the new text’s length, the `secret` choice, or even the item/kind, despite the adjacent comment saying the secret correction “binds the text’s length and the secret choice instead.” For example, after requesting approval for `--field body --secret --text a --reason r`, the recorded `state` digest is the same as for a re-run of the same approval with `--field body --secret --text aaaaaaaaaa --reason r` (or, depending on the gate, another record with the same field names), because only `names` is digested. The length/choice are only placed in `args`; the digest that the comment says the ask records does not change, so the approval is not bound to the correction the operator approved.

For example, `ddflow correct BUG-1 --field body --from-file bad.bin --reason "wrong"` with a non-text/binary file will escape this helper as an unhandled exception instead of returning the intended `cannot read ...` failure.

chunk_findings.detail: The new help paragraph claims CLI/MCP parity from one declaration, but the documented MCP action list omits `from_file` while the CLI examples immediately above use `--from-file`. An MCP caller following the documented parameters (`id`, `field`, `text`, `reason`, `kind`, `secret`, `approval`) has no way to supply the file-backed input path that the CLI surface supports. If the declared `correct` action actually exposes `from_file`, this help text is wrong and will fail the help/README parity acceptance; if it does not, then the declared command is not the CLI/MCP parity promised by the intent.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/prompts/help/update.md:35

chunk_findings.detail: The second part of this test calls the MCP alias `ddflow_correct` and only asserts `not bad`; it never asserts that the alias actually changed the record or emitted a second `record.corrected` event. If the alias is registered in `TOOLS`/`F.ALIASES` but its handler is a no-op or updates the wrong record while returning a successful MCP result, the test still passes, so it does not establish CLI/MCP parity for the alias. Given a `ddflow_correct` alias that returns `{"ok": true}` without modifying `B1`, the assertions after the first `ddflow_task` call still pass and the alias call’s `not bad` check still passes, leaving the broken alias untested.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_record_correct_surface.py:test_cli_and_mcp_are_one_declaration

chunk_findings.detail: The changed binary-file refusal still violates the stated “every refusal names the nearest verb” rule. For the input used by the new test, `ddflow correct B1 --field summary --from-file bad.bin --reason r`, `Path.read_text()` raises `UnicodeDecodeError`, the new `except` returns the refusal text `cannot read bad.bin as text: ...`, and that is what the CLI surfaces as the failure. Unlike the API refusals fixed in this commit, this refusal does not include `NEAREST` (`ddflow correct <id> --field NAME --text TEXT --reason WHY`); the added test only checks for “as text” and the absence of a traceback, so it does not cover the missing nearest verb.

chunk_findings.detail: For `secret= [REDACTED] the code computes `bound = D.content_digest(names)`, which does not bind the new text’s length, the `secret` choice, or even the item/kind, despite the adjacent comment saying the secret correction “binds the text’s length and the secret choice instead.” For example, after requesting approval for `--field body --secret --text a --reason r`, the recorded `state` digest is the same as for a re-run of the same approval with `--field body --secret --text aaaaaaaaaa --reason r` (or, depending on the gate, another record with the same field names), because only `names` is digested. The length/choice are only placed in `args`; the digest that the comment says the ask records does not change, so the approval is not bound to the correction the operator approved.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/record_correct.py:_permission (`bound` secret branch)

chunk_findings.detail: The changed approval-site description says the T2 ask carries “the new text,” but `_permission` passes no new text to `operator_gate`: the `Canon` it builds contains only `kind`, `reason`, `secret`, `chars`, and a digest in `state`. Given a non-secret correction that needs approval, e.g. `ddflow correct B1 --field body --text 'fix typo' --reason 'typo' --approval request`, the ask cannot show `fix typo`; it can only show its digest and length. The site metadata therefore misstates what the operator is being asked to approve.
